core.title: Cached or incremental results: place cache work within implemented runtime
core.given: Work reuses or incrementally recomputes an expensive, repeatable read or derivation with stable identities and tractable dependencies
core.when: deciding where the cache work or hit/miss routing runs
core.then: Do not treat this pattern as providing a new runtime dispatch option, and do not plan on orchestration behavior inferred from it that is not implemented.
prefer: Cache work can be internal to an already-implemented unit of the product.
An explicit hit/miss route can use an existing, already-implemented mechanism.
avoid: Citing this pattern as providing or authorizing a new runtime dispatch option for cache hit/miss.
Relying on unimplemented orchestration behavior inferred from this pattern.
core.why: The pattern is guidance only; plans that assume dispatch or orchestration that does not exist cannot run.
evidence: Planned cache placement does not rely on this pattern as the source of any new runtime dispatch option (placements the pattern names include cache work internal to an already-implemented unit of the product, or an explicit hit/miss route using an existing, already-implemented mechanism; these are examples, not an exhaustive or mandatory list).
The plan relies on no orchestration behavior that is unimplemented and only inferred from this pattern.
verification: Advisory pattern guidance (severity 3, disposition advisory); not independent enforcement — existing plan and source validators apply.
Flag reliance on unimplemented orchestration behavior inferred from this pattern; such behavior cannot be inferred from a pattern.
Activation requires the finding fact and applies no phase restriction; the task-term fact is an optional hint only.

values: placement of cache/incremental work or a hit/miss route for an expensive repeatable result with stable identity and tractable dependencies

fires: Deciding whether cache work lives inside an already-implemented unit of the product or behind an explicit hit/miss route.
A plan proposes an explicit hit/miss route for a reused result.
doesNotFire: Work outside the applicability criteria of this pattern.

bunOnly.text: Cache work can be internal to a wagon.
bunOnly.reason: 'wagon' is the stack's bounded-slice layout concept (layout.wagon_dir in profile terms); it is a structure name, not a role, and bun.json supplies no concrete value a profile key could cite. The core states the placement neutrally as an already-implemented unit of the product; each realization instantiates the example from its own layout.

bunOnly.text: An explicit hit/miss route can use an existing interlocking.
bunOnly.reason: 'interlocking' is a stack coordination/dispatch construct with no key in the closed vocabulary and no role-level equivalent; the core says 'an existing, already-implemented mechanism'.

bunOnly.text: placements the pattern names include cache work internal to a wagon, or an explicit hit/miss route using an existing interlocking
bunOnly.reason: The parenthetical names the two stack-concrete example placements ('wagon', 'interlocking'); the core keeps the same two example shapes in neutral wording plus the 'examples, not an exhaustive or mandatory list' qualifier.
A stack-specific task term in the optional activation hint; the neutral core keeps only the generic cache terms (cache, hit/miss, incremental, reuse).
A realization-specific shared-policy reference id; per the notProfileKeys rule such ids stay with the realization, and the core's verification states the advisory scope generically.

classification.note: Single obligation carried verbatim; both halves (no new runtime dispatch option; no unimplemented orchestration) are kept — nothing dropped or added.
Neutralized: 'wagon' becomes 'an already-implemented unit of the product'; the concrete Bun placement example is realization-only.
Neutral evidence obligation kept; only the two named example placements are restated in role-neutral wording, preserving the 'examples, not exhaustive or mandatory' qualifier.

Severity 3 / advisory disposition and the 'not independent enforcement; existing plan and source validators apply' scope go to core verification; the shared:policy.pattern-guidance id is realization-only.
Generic check description: flag reliance on unimplemented orchestration behavior inferred from the pattern.
Finding fact carried verbatim (neutral, llm_judged); its 'REQUIRED. No phase restriction.' note is preserved in core verification.
Generic task terms kept; the stack term 'interlocking' is Bun-only; the 'OPTIONAL hint only.' note is preserved in core verification.

neutralityNotes: The core needs no profile values: bun.json names no stack, tool, path or suffix — its only stack-specific content is the vocabulary 'wagon' (bounded product slice) and 'interlocking' (existing coordination/dispatch construct), plus the shared:policy.pattern-guidance reference; all are carried in bunOnly, so profileRequirements and proposedKeys are empty. activation.fires[0] ('inside a wagon') was neutralized the same way as prefer[0] ('inside an already-implemented unit of the product'). The fact-level notes (REQUIRED/no phase restriction; OPTIONAL hint only) moved into core verification because the neutral fact schema carries no note field. 'unless' is empty in bun.json and stays empty — no exception dropped or added. The severity-3 advisory disposition stays in core verification, not the profile.
